result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick the sidebar, explain why tabs and one long page lose, and give a drill-down list layout for phones, so they are very close. A edges ahead on rubric item 4: it says the team and vehicles tables can run wider than the form cap, and it limits in-page anchors to long groups. B handles big groups only through card grids and tables. B's search field and merged groups are good ideas, but the rubric doesn't score them. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick the sidebar, use drill-down lists on phones and give similar reasons for rejecting tabs and the long page. B is slightly more buildable: it gives a sticky sidebar and a 40–60ch field cap, explicitly lets the data tables run wider than the forms, and plans for per-integration sub-pages. A has useful touches of its own, such as merging the groups, adding search and showing summary lines on mobile rows. B handles the large groups and the rejected options in a bit more depth.
